उच्चैःश्रवस्: Uccaiḥśravas m.: A mythical horse. A. Origin: Narrated in the आस्तीकपर्वन् 1. 2. 73; arose from the ocean when it was churned for nectar (अमृत) 1. 15. 2; 1. 16. 34; 5. 100. 12; 6. 32. 27. B. Description and Status: White and lustrous (पाण्डुर, महाद्युति), king of horses (अश्वराज), jewel among horses (अश्वरत्न, अश्वानां वर); heavenly, unaging, having the strength of a torrent (महौघबल), very speedy (मनोजव, अतुलविक्रम), marked by all good signs, honoured by hosts of gods 1. 15. 2-4; 1. 16. 34, 36; 1. 18. 1; 8. 5. 21. C. Myth: Seen by sisters Kadrū and Vinatā from near 1. 15. 1; Kadrū challenged Vinatā to tell quickly the colour of Uccaiḥśravas; Vinatā described it to be white and asked Kadrū what she thought about it; Kadrū said Ucchaiḥśravas had a black tail; both agree to a wager on it—one who loses shall be the दासी of the winner (अत्र विपणावहे; दीव्य दासीभावाय) 1. 18. 1-5; next morning when they went to see the horse from near they found many dark hair sticking to its tail 1. 19. 1-2; 1. 20. 2; 1. 49. 6. D. Greatness: considered as one of the विभूतिस् of Bhagavān 6 32. 27; even Uccaiḥśravas to be given as gift to a deserving person 12. 226. 15. E. Standard of comparison: Aśvatthām-an. as soon as born, neighed loudly like Uccaiḥśravas 1. 121. 13; 7. 167. 29; Kṛṣṇa, as a child killed a horse as strong as Uccaiḥ-śravas 7. 10. 3; dust raised by the Aśvamedha horse was like the one raised by Uccaiḥśravas 14. 89. 16
उच्छिख: Ucchikha m.: A mythical serpent, born in the कुल of Takṣaka, one of those offered in the सर्पसत्र 1. 52. 8, 7, 9.
उद्रपारग: Udrapāraga: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, one of those offered in the सर्पसत्र; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग) and ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 15, 1, 13.
उपतक्षक: Upatakṣaka m.: A mythical serpent. One of the sons of Kadrū, he took the side of Arjuna when those who had gathered in the mid-region took sides between Karṇa and Arjuna 8. 63. 36, 30-31.
उपनन्दक: Upanandaka m.: A mythical serpent, living in Bhogavatī Purī 5. 101. 12, 1. Son of Surasā and Kaśyapa 5. 101. 4, 17; description 5. 101. 5-7.

Upanandaka m. (pl.): Name of a class of warriors. On the second day of war, Duryodhana asked Upanandakas, led by Duḥśāsana and Vikarṇa, to protect Bhīṣma (दुःशा-सनेन च । विकर्णेन च वीरेण तथा नन्दोपनन्दकैः … सहिताः … भीष्मम् एवाभिरक्षन्तु) 6. 47. 8-9.
उलूक: Ulūka m.: A mythical bird ? Garuḍa tore him apart with nails and beak while on his expedition to fetch अमृत 1. 28. 19, 20. [Name of a Yakṣa according to Nīlakaṇṭha].
उलूपी: Ulūpī f.: A Nāga princess (पन्नगी 1. 206. 18; भुजङ्गमा 1. 206. 23). A. Early life: Daughter of Nāgarāja Airāvata (daughter not named here, but appa-rently identical with Ulūpī); married first to a नाग who was killed by Suparṇa; she had no child; next, given by her father as wife to Arjuna 6. 86. 6-8; her son Irāvant called a दायाद of Arjuna 6. 86. 11; yet Irāvant described as the son fathered by Arjuna on the wife of another person (परक्षेत्र) 6. 86. 11 [apparently परक्षेत्र here intended to mean that Ulūpī was a widow when married to Arjuna; no mention in this narration of Ulūpī's amorous advance (साहस) to Arjuna 1. 206. 17.] B. Meeting with Arjuna: described in the अर्जुनवनवासपर्वन् 1. 2. 91 = 1. 206; she saw Arjuna while bathing in Gaṅgā; fell in love with him and dragged him into water; on enquiry she told Arjuna she was the daughter of the serpent (पन्नग) Kauravya born in the family of Airāvata; she requested Arjuna to make her happy by uniting with her; she pleaded that he would not thereby violate his vow to observe celibacy for twelve years since, by uniting with her, he would be offering protection to the distressed and would be saving her life; Arjuna agreed to her request 1. 206. 13-33 [No mention in this narration of Arjuna's marrying her]. C. Role in Arjuna's battle with Babhruvāhana: Ulūpī enraged when Arjuna rebuked her ‘son’ Babhruvāhana for not offering a fight; she who was versed in the duties of a Kṣatriya (क्षात्रधर्मविशारदा 14. 78. 10), therefore broke open the earth and appeared on the scene; she introduced herself to Babhruvāhana as his mother and asked him to fight with Arjuna 14. 78. 8-13; Citrāṅgadā, mistaking Arjuna and Babhruvāhana to be dead when they fell unconscious on the ground in the armed conflict that followed, scolded Ulūpī for inciting Babhruvāhana to offer a fight; she requested Ulūpī to bring Arjuna to life, not minding the death of Babhruvāhana 14. 79. 2-7, 12-17; Babh-ruvāhana, on gaining consciousness scolded Ulūpī for the same reason 14. 80. 13-15; Ulūpī told Babhruvāhana that Arjuna was not really dead but was in a swoon as she had employed मोहिनी माया; she asked Babhruvāhana to fight because Arjuna wanted to put his strength to test; she then thought of the सङ्जीवन मणि and asked Babhruvāhana to place it on Arjuna's chest to bring him back to consciousness 14. 81. 2, 4-7, 9-10; Arjuna, when revived, asked Ulūpī the reason for her presence on the battle-field 14. 82. 1-4; she told Arjuna that what she did was for the atonement (निष्कृति) and pacification (शान्ति) through his son for his sinful act in felling down Bhīṣma in an unlawful way (अधर्मेण) 14. 82. 8-11; when Bhīṣma fell, Vasus cursed Arjuna, where-upon Ulūpī requested her father to intercede on behalf of Arjuna; Ulūpī's inciting Babhru-vāhana was to release Arjuna from that curse; Arjuna expressed satisfaction at what Ulūpī had done 14. 82. 15-22; Arjuna invited Babhruvāhana to attend the Aśvamedha with his two mothers (Ulūpī and Citrāṅgadā) and took leave of his wives 14. 82. 24, 32. D. Later life and End: She was one of those who waited on Gāndhārī 15. 1. 21; Sāmba, a Brāhmaṇa assured Dhṛtarāṣṭra on behalf of his subjects that neither Kuntī, nor Draupadī, nor Ulūpī, nor Subhadrā would do anything harmful to the people 15. 16. 20; she entered Gaṅgā when the Pāṇḍavas finally left Hās-tinapura 17. 1. 25. E. Epithets: पन्न-गात्मजा (and synonymous expressions) 14. 78. 11; 14. 79. 7, 8; 14. 79. 2, 18; 14. 82. 2; 17. 1. 25; 14. 78. 10; 14. 82. 5; नागराज-सुता (and its synonyms) 1. 206. 16; 6. 86. 6; 14. 80. 13; 1. 206. 33; 14. 81. 3; भुजगोत्तमा 14. 80. 17; कौरव्यदुहिता 14. 82. 23; कौरव्यकुलनन्दिनी 14. 82. 1; जलचारिणी 1. 206. 33; देवी 14. 79. 8.
उद्भ्रान्त: Udbhrānta nt.: One of the twenty-one movements (मार्ग) used while fighting with a sword. Dhṛṣtadyumna adopted it in turn while attacking Droṇa 7. 164. 147-148.
उपनन्द: Upananda m.: Name of a drum (मृदङ्ग). One of the two drums (the other being Nanda) of appropriate size, producing sweet sound at the crest of the flag of Yudhiṣṭhira (यस्य ध्वजाग्रे नदतो मृदङ्गौ नन्दो-पनन्दौ मधुरौ युक्तरूपौ) 3. 254. 6.
उद्योगपर्वन्: Udyogaparvan1 nt.: Name of the 49th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 49, 33, 70. Described as highly wonderful (महा-द्भुत) 1. 2. 49; alluded to briefly in the narration of the contents of the Udyoga-parvan—where Duryodhana and Arjuna waited on Vāsudeva (Kṛṣṇa) for help in the ensuing war and where Duryodhana opted for the army, अक्षौहिणी strong, of Kṛṣṇa, while Arjuna opted for Kṛṣṇa as a non-combatant counsellor (अयुध्यमानं सचिवं) 1. 2. 136-139; (also 1. 1. 118); it comprises अध्यायस् 5. 1-21.

Udyogaparvan,2 Udyoga nt.: Name of the fifth पर्वन् in the list of the eighteen major पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata 1. 2. 136, 151, 71; called Udyoga (for short) 6. 41. 81; 6. 95. 11. It contains many events (सुबहुवृत्तान्त) and is concerned with the efforts for peace and war (संधिविग्रहसंश्रित) 1. 2. 151; according to the Parvasaṃgraha it has 186 अध्यायस् and 6698 श्लोकस् as told by Vyāsa (प्रोक्ताः … महात्मना । व्यासेनोदार-मतिना) 1. 2. 152-153; summary of its con-tents: when the Pāṇḍavas resided in Upa-plavya, Duryodhana and Arjuna approached Vāsudeva (Kṛṣṇa) to seek his help in the com-ing war; when Kṛṣṇa asked them to choose between himself and his army, Duryodhana chose the latter, while Dhanaṃjaya chose the former; Dhṛtarāṣṭra sent Saṃjaya as his envoy to the Pāṇḍavas for conciliation; Dhṛta-rāṣṭra having come to know (from Saṃjaya) that the Pāṇḍavas would be led by Kṛṣṇa lost sleep due to anxiety; Vidura gave Dhṛta-rāṣṭra much sound advice; the sage Sanat-sujāta gave him an excellent discourse on the doctrine of soul (अध्यात्मम् अनुत्त-मम् … श्रावितः); Saṃjaya told Dhṛta-rāṣṭra about the close association of Vāsu-deva and Arjuna; Kṛṣṇa himself left for Hāstinapura to seek conciliation with the Kauravas; Duryodhana's rejection of Kṛṣṇa's proposal which would be for the benefit of both the parties; Kṛṣṇa sensing the evil intention of Karṇa, Duryodhana and the rest (to imprison him) displayed his prowess as a योगेश्वर to the kings; Kṛṣṇa tried to win over Karṇa to the side of the Pāṇḍavas but Karṇa, due to his sense of pride, did not oblige; the army consisting of chariots, horses, soldiers and elephants, marched out of Hāstinapura; counting of the forces; Ulūka sent as a messenger to the Pāṇḍavas a day before the war; counting of the रथिन्स् and अतिरथिन्स्; the narrative of Ambā 1. 2. 136-150 (also 1. 1. 116-120); Yudhiṣṭhira asked Śalya to fulfil the boon he gave to Yudhiṣṭhira in the Udyoga (i. e. in the Udyogaparvan) and weaken the vigour (तेजोवध) of Karṇa during the war (a reference to 5. 18. 22-24) 6. 41. 81; that Śikhaṇḍin was first born as a woman was told by Bhīṣma in the Udyoga (reference to 5. 189-193) 6. 95. 11.
उलूकदूतागमन: Ulūkadūtāgamana (also known as Ulūkayāna) nt.: Name of the 58th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 53, 33, 70. Counted in the contents of the Udyoga-parvan; it relates to the dispatch Ulūka as a messenger to the Pāṇḍavas on the eve of the battle 1. 2. 150; comprises अध्यायस् 5. 157-161.
उत्तर: Uttara Proṣṭhapada m.: Name of a नक्षत्र। [See Uttarā Bhādrapadā]

Uttara m. (pl.): Name of a people ? Bhīma in his expedition to the east, south, and north before the Rājasūya con-quered the Uttaras along with the Uttamas (सोत्तमान् अपि चोत्तरान् । … व्यजयत् प्र-भुः) 2. 27. 3; (for other references and an alternative explanation of the word see Uttama).
उत्तरा: Uttarā Phalgunī f. (sg., du, pl.): Name of a नक्षत्र। A. Epic event: Arjuna was born on the mountain Himavant under the junction of the two constellations Pūrvā and Uttarā Phalgunī, hence called Phalguna (उत्तरा-भ्यां च पूर्वाभ्यां फल्गुनीभ्याम् अहं दिवा । जातो हिमवतः पृष्ठे तेन मां फल्गुनं विदुः) 4. 39. 14. (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 4. 44. 16: उत्तराभ्यां च पूर्वाभ्याम् इति पाठे नक्षत्रसन्धौ इत्य् अर्थः). B. Religious rites: Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that if, after ob-serving fast (उपोषितः 13. 63. 13), one gave, according to the rites (विधिवत्), under this नक्षत्र (उत्तराविषये) gift of cooked rice made of grains that ripen in sixty days (षष्टि-कौदन) mixed with घृत and milk, he was honoured in heaven 13. 63. 14; whatever gift one gave under this नक्षत्र it produced ample benefit that became everlasting (यद् यत् प्रदीयते दानम् उत्त्राविषये नरैः । महाफलम् अनतं च भवतीति विनिश्-चयः) 13. 63. 15; Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that if one offered a काम्य श्राद्ध under this नक्षत्र one got progeny (अपत्य-भाग् उत्तरासु) 13. 89. 6.

Uttarā Bhādrapadā f. (sg., pl), Uttara Proṣṭhapada m. (sg.): Name of a con-stellation. A. Religious rites: Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that if one gave as a gift meat of a ram or a sheep under the conste-llation Uttarā Bhādrapadā he gave delight to the manes and obtained infinite (happiness) after death (औरभ्रम् उत्तरायोगे यस् तु मांसं प्रयच्छति । स पितॄन् प्रीणयति वै प्रेत्य चानन्त्यम् अश्नुते) 13. 63. 32; Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that by offering a काम्य श्राद्ध under this नक्षत्र one got a thousand cows (उत्तरास्व् अथ कुर्वाणः) 13. 89. 13. B. Bad omens: Among the bad omens which oc-curred before the start of the war and which were reported by Vyāsa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra there was one according to which the planet Śukra after ascending Pūrva Proṣṭhapada and then having gone to the Uttara Proṣṭhapada was, together with it (?) looking back at (the Pūrva Preṣṭhapada) (शुक्रः प्रोष्ठ-पदे पूर्वे समारुह्य विशां पते । उत्तरे तु परिक्रम्य सहितः प्रत्युदीक्षते ॥ ) 6. 3. 14 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. on 6. 3. 15: पूर्वे प्रोष्ठपदे पूर्वाभाद्रपदा-नक्षत्रं समारुह्य परिक्रम्य परि-घाख्य उपग्रहस् तेन सहितः उत्तरे उत्तराभाद्रपदानक्षत्रम् उदीक्षते आक्रा-न्तुम् इच्छति).
उत्तरायण: Uttarāyaṇa nt.: Name of the period in which the sun moves to the north, the summer solstice; also called Udagā̆yana (-आ- म्। च्।) (6. 114. 98; 12. 224. 16). A. Sun's courses fixed by Brahman: Śakra told Bali that the self-born god (Sva-yaṃbhū) had fixed the movements of the sun following which the sun moved towards the north for six months and towards the south for six months 12. 218. 35-36. B. Its duration: The calculators of the divi-sions of time say that the year consists of two अयनस् (sun's courses), viz. दक्षिण and उत्तर (संवतसरं द्वे अयने वदन्ति संख्याविदो दक्षिणम् उत्तरम् च) 12. 224. 13; (12. 47. 42); 13. 16. 46; Nārada told Devamata that the two अयनस् (दक्षिण and उत्तर) form a pair and between them is fire; Brāhmaṇas knew that that is the highest form of उदान (? उभे चैवायने द्वंद्वं तयोर् मध्ये हुताशनः । एतद् रूपम् उदानस्य परमं ब्राह्मना विदुः) 14. 24. 15; Vyāsa had told Śuka that the night and the day of the gods was equal to one human year of which the उत्तरायण form-ed the day and the दक्षिणायन the night (दैवे रात्र्यहनी वर्षम् प्रविभागस् तयोः पुनः । अहस् तत्रोदगयनं रात्रिः स्याद् दक्षिणायनम्) 12. 224. 16. C. Effects on the earth: The sun, during its two courses, northern and southern, distributes cold and heat among the people (अयनं तस्य षण्मासा उत्तरं दक्षिणं तथा । येन संयाति लोकेषु शीतोष्णे विसृजन् रविः ॥ ) 12. 218. 36; the sun, having traversed its northern course and having collected with his rays the heated waters, turns for the southern course and enters the earth; there, lying in the earth and sprinkled with the energies of the moon, it produces plants which serve as food for living beings (गत्वोत्तरायणं तेजोरसान् उद्धृत्य रश्मिभिः । दक्षिणा-यनम् आवृत्तो महीं निविशते रविः ॥ … निषिक्तश् चन्द्रतेजोभिः सूयते भूगतो रविः । ओषध्यः षड्रसा मेध्यास् तद् अन्नं प्राणिनां भुवि ॥ ) 3. 3. 6, 8 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 3. 6: तेजोरसान् जलानि). D. Importance: Mahādeva (13. 16. 13) identified with both the Uttara and the Dakṣiṇa ayana 13. 16. 46. E. Considered holy: The night in the Uttarāyaṇa is con-sidered holy and divine; Śacī bowed down to this goddess Rātri so that her wish to see her husband was fulfilled (पुण्यां चेमाम् अहं दिव्यां प्रवृत्ताम् उत्तरायणे । देवीं रात्रिम् नमस्यामि सिध्यतां मे मनोर-थः ॥ ) 5. 13. 23; from Dakṣiṇāyana (which symbolizes darkness) proceeds Uttarāyaṇa (which stands for light); (hence) the gift of light is praiseworthy (अन्धं तमस् तमि-स्रं च दक्षिणायनम् एव च । उत्तरायणम् एतस्माज् ज्योतिर्दानं प्रशस्यते ॥ ) 13. 101. 46 (perhaps what is meant is that giving gifts of light helps the bringing in of the Uttarāyaṇa. Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 98. 47: तमिस्रं अन्धकारः । अन्धंतमो नाम नरकरूपं तथा दक्षिणायनम् अप्य् अन्धंतम एव । अत उत्तरायणे रात्रौ तमोनाशकं ज्योतिर् देयं नरकनिवृत्त्यर्-थम्। Editor, Cr. Ed., Vol. 17. (part II), p. 1098 on 13. 101. 46, however,: “Does this suggest the origin of the Dīpāvali festival ?”). F. Bhīṣma's death in Uttarāyaṇa: Bhīṣma when he fell on the ground in the war did not give up his life as he wished to wait till the setting in of the Uttarāyaṇa 6. 114. 89; he assured the sages, sent to him by Gaṅgā, when they came to him in the form of swans, that he would sustain his life and go to his ori-ginal place when the sun had turned towards the north 6. 114. 97; he told them that he would sustain his life longing for the Uttarā-yaṇa; established in complete sway (over his life), he could control the act of giving up life; he would therefore hold life for some time since he wished to die in the Udagāyana (धारयिष्याम्य् अहं प्राणान् उत्तरायण-काङ्क्षया । ऐश्वर्यभूतः प्राणानाम् उत्सर्गे नियतो ह्य् अहम् । तस्मात् प्राणान् धारयिष्ये मुमूर्षुर् उदगायने ॥ ) 6. 114. 98 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 119. 106: स्वसामर्थ्येन भूतः प्राप्तः स्वच्छ-न्दमृत्युत्वात्); Bhīṣma's future death in the Uttarāyaṇa alluded to by Yudhiṣṭhira 12. 291. 4 (आवृत्ते भगवत्य् अर्के गनतासि पर-मां गतिम्); Bhīṣma asked Yudhiṣṭhira to come back to him when the sun had returned from the Dakṣiṇāyana and the Uttarāyaṇa had set in 13. 152. 10; when the Uttarāyaṇa set in, Yudhiṣṭhira started from Hāstinapura to meet Bhīṣma (for the remembered what Bhīṣma had told him) 13. 153. 6; Bhīṣma greeted Yudhiṣṭhira and said that the sun had turned back (from the Dakṣināyana) 13. 153. 26; as soon as the sun had returned to its northerly course Bhīṣma, well composed, placed himself in his soul (to he ready to abandon the body) 12. 47. 3; Bhīṣma gave up his life when the Uttarāyaṇa had set in 14. 59. 12.
उत्तराषाढा: Uttarāṣāḍhā f. (pl.): Name of a con-stellation. Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that if one gave under the Uttarā Aṣāḍhā a pot of barley-preparation (?) mixed with clarified butter and thickened with plenty of honey one obtained all desires 13. 63. 26. (उदमन्-थं ससर्पिष्कं प्रभूतमधुफाणि-तम् । दत्त्वोत्तरास्व् अषाढासु सर्वकामान् अवाप्नुयात् ॥ Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 64. 26: (उदमन्थम्) उदकुंभयुक्तं सक्तु-विकारम्; Unknown commentator: उदमन्-थं नवनीतम्, cf. Cr. Ed., Vol. 17, part II. p. 1080 note on 13. 63. 26); Yama told Śaśa-bindu (13. 89. 1) that by offering a काम्य श्राद्ध under the Uttarā Aṣāḍhā one was freed of all sorrow (उत्तरासु त्व् अषाढासु वीतशोकश् चरेन् महीम्) 13. 89. 10.
उज्जयन्त: Ujjayanta m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: Situated in the Surāṣṭras 3. 86. 20, 16. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) and inhabited by animals and birds (मृगपक्षिणिषेवित) 3. 86. 20; great, having summits, and one that brings success quickly (उज्जयन्तश् च शिखरी क्षिप्रं सिद्धिकरो महान्) 3. 86. 18. C. Importance: Dhau-mya informed Yudhiṣṭhira about an ancient stanza (पुराणः श्लोकः) about this mountain sung by Nārada (नारदेनानुकीर्तितः); ac-cording to it one who practised austerities on the mountain Ujjayanta was glorified in the heaven (उज्जयन्ते स्म तप्ताङ्गो नाकपृष्ठे महीयते) 3. 86. 20 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 88. 23: तप्ताङ्गः कृतततपस्कः).
उज्जानक: Ujjānaka1 m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the आश्रमस् of Ārṣṭiṣena and Piṅgā; by bathing (उपस्पृश्य) there one became free of sins 13. 26. 52. [See Ujjā-naka2]

Ujjānaka2 m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Seems to be different from Ujjānaka1; situated not far from the Vātikaṣaṇḍa which lay to the north of the Videha country (एष वातिकषण्डो वै … विदेहान् उत्तरश् च यः । एष उज्जानको नाम) 3. 130. 13-14; here Yavakrī obtained peace and also the sage Vasiṣṭha in the company of Arundhatī (एष उज्जानको नाम यवक्रीर् यत्र शान्तवान् । अरुन्धतीसहायश् च वसिष्ठो भगवान् ऋषिः) 3. 130. 14. [See Ujjānaka1]

Ujjānaka3 m.: Name of a desert. A. Location: Situated on an even waste land near the आश्रम of Uttaṅka (ममाश्रमसमीपे (i. e. Uttaṅkasya) वै समेषु मरुधन्वसु) 3. 193. 14. B. Description: A sea full of sand (समुद्रो वालुकापुर्ण उज्जानक इति स्मृतः) 3. 193. 15; 3. 195. 7; it was many योजनस् long and many योजनस् wide (बहुयोजनविस्तीर्णो बहुयोजनम् आयतः) 3. 193. 15. C. Event: A Dānava named Dhundhu lived there underground concealed in sand (अन्तर् भूमिगतो राजन् वसति) 3. 193. 16-17; (अन्तर् भूमिगतस् तत्र वालुकान्तर्हितस् तदा) 3. 195. 8; Dhundhu caused disturbance to the आश्रम of Uttaṅka 3. 195. 7.
उत्कोचक: Utkocaka nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Dhaumya, the younger brother of Devala, had his आश्रम near this तीर्थ where he practised austerities; Pāṇḍavas, as advised by the Gandharva, went to this तीर्थ and chose Dhaumya for their priest 1. 174. 2; 1. 174. 6 (तत उत्कोचकं तीर्थं गत्वा धौ-म्याश्रमं तु ते । तं वव्रुः पाण्डवा धौम्यं पौरोहित्याय भारत).
उत्तरमानस: Uttaramānasa nt.: Name of a lake. Mentioned along with Puṣkara and Pra-bhāsa 12. 148. 11; after visiting these lakes one again obtains long life in this life (लब्-धायुर्जीविते पुनः) 12. 148. 11.
उत्पलावत: Utpalāvata nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: Located near Kanya-kubja in the Pāñcālas 3. 85. 12, 11. B. Past event: It was here that Viśvāmitra, the Kauśika, offered sacrifice to Indra (विश्वा-मित्रो ऽयजद् यत्र शक्रेण सह कौशिकः) 3. 85. 11; having seen Viśvāmitra's super-human power (Rāma) Jāmadagnya sang a family-related (stanza) (अनुवंश): “Kauśika drank सोम with Indra at Kanya-kubja; he then left his royal status and declared: ‘I am a Brāhmaṇa’” (यत्रानु-वंशं भगवाञ् जामदग्न्यस् तथा जगौ ॥ विश्वामित्रस्य तां दृष्ट्वा विभूतिम् अतिमानुषीम् । कन्यकुब्जे ऽपिबत् सोमम् इन्द्रेण सह कौशिकः । ततः क्षत्राद् अपाक्रामद् ब्राह्मणो ऽस्मीति चाब्रवीत् ॥ ) 3. 85. 11-12.
उत्पलावती: Utpalāvatī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 33, 5; its water used for drinking by the people 6. 10. 13; all these rivers are described as mothers of the universe (विश्वस्य मातरः) and very strong (महा-बलाः) 6. 10. 35.
उत्पलावन: Utpalāvana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। If one bathes there (? offers libations to the पितृस् ?) (कृतोदकः) for a month, he obtains the fruit of performing an Aśvamedha sacrifice 13. 26. 33.
उत्पलिनी: Utpalinī f.: Name of a river. After coming down from the Himālayas and while proceeding towards the east, Arjuna first saw the beautiful (रम्या) river Utaplinī near the Naimiṣa forest 1. 207. 6.
उदपान: Udapāna1 m.: Name (?) of a well (कूप). A. Location: Situated near Śālagrāma, sacred to Viṣṇu 3. 82. 106. B. Descrip-tion: Capable of freeing of all sins (सर्व-पापप्रमोचन) 3. 82. 108. C. Im-portance: All the four oceans are always present in this well (समुद्रास् तत्र चत्-वारः कूपे संनिहिताः सदा) 3. 82. 108; if one bathed (उपस्पृश्य) there one did not meet with calamities (न दुर्गतिम् अवाप्-नुयात्) 3. 82. 108; by approaching (अभि-गम्य) the great god Viṣṇu there one shines like Soma being freed of all debts (विराजति यथा सोम ऋणैर् मुक्तो युधिष्ठिर) 3. 82. 109. [See Kūpa1 and Kūpa2]

Udapāna2 m.: Name (?) of a well. Balarāma went there from the Cama-sodbheda तीर्थ; since it is an excellent means of acquiring well-being and great merit and since the plants and the earth there look glossy, the Siddhas know the river Sarasvatī, although not visible, to be present there (आद्यं स्वस्त्ययनं चैव तत्रावाप्य महत् फलम् ॥ स्निग्धत्वाद् ओषढीनां च भूमेश् च जनमेजय । जानन्ति सिद्धा राजेन्द्र नष्टाम् अपि सरस्वतीम् ॥ ) 9. 34. 80-81. [See Udapāna, Kūpa]

Udapāna3 m.: The well of Trita. A. Location: Situated on the bank of the river Sarasvatī 9. 35. 24, hence called नदीगत 9. 35. 1, 53. B. Description: Great (महत्) 9. 35. 24; very deep (अगाध) and extremely terrible (सुमहाघोर) 3. 35. 25; without water (निर्जल), hence covered with soil (पांसुस्ंवृत, पांसुग्रस्त) 9. 35. 28, 32; covered with plants and grass (वीरुत्तृणावृत) 9. 35. 29; frightful to all creatures (सर्वभूतभयङ्कर, प्रति-भय) 9. 35. 25, 42. C. Events: (1) Epic: Balarāma bathed there and gave ample wealth to Brāhmaṇas and worshipped them 9. 35. 2, 52; he praised the तीर्थ and left for Vinaśanatīrtha 9. 35. 53; (2) Of the past Yuga (9. 35. 7): Trita, afraid of a wolf, fell into this well; his two brothers, Ekata and Dvita (9. 35. 7), deserted him there and went home (9. 35. 25, 27, 4-6); he, by chance, saw a plant in the well (9. 35. 31); using it as a Soma plant, Trita offered a sacrifice in the well and drank Soma (9. 35. 32-35, 3); gods came to the well, where Trita was consecrated for the sacrifice, to receive their shares (9. 35. 40); Trita asked the following boon from the gods: One who bathes in this well shall obtain the same condition after death as one who has (offered a Soma sacrifice and) drunk Soma (यश् चेहोपस्पृशेत् कूपे स सोमपगतिं लभेत्) 9. 35. 45; at that moment Sarasvatī sprang up in the well and brought Trita out of the well 9. 35. 46. D. Simile: Trita's falling down in the well compared to a sinner's falling in the Naraka 9. 35. 29.
उदय: Udaya m.: Name of the eastern moun-tain from behind which the sun rises. A. Mythological event: Indra, in con-versation with Devasenā, saw the sun on the Udaya mountain and the moon entering the sun; at that point when the Raudra मुहूर्त commenced on the new moon day he saw the battle raging between gods and demons on the Udaya mountain (अमावास्यां संप्रवृत्तं मुहूर्तं रौद्रम् एव च । देवासुरं च संग्रामं सो ऽपश्यद् उदये गिरौ) 3. 213. 26-27. B. Similes: (1) Śālva mounted on his elephant appeared like the sun on the Udaya mountain at the end of the night 9. 19. 4; (2) Arjuna mounted his excellent chariot as does the sun the Udaya 7. 60. 16; (3) Karṇa, shining with his white splendour (कर्णम् … श्वेतच्छ-विविराजितम्), appeared like the sun beautify-ing the Udaya mountain 8. 43. 38; (4) The elephant, fierce and properly equipped, on which Bhīma had mounted, looked like a man-sion on the topmost part of the Udaya where the sun had arisen (उदयाग्र्यभवनं यथाभ्युदितभास्करम्) 8. 8. 22; (5) Kṛṣṇa, with the Kaustubha jewel shining on his chest, looked like the Udaya mountain with the rising sun 12. 45. 15; (6) Duryo-dhana and Śalya received the attacking warriors like the Asta and the Udaya moun-tains receiving the huge clouds 9. 15. 31; (7) Just as an object on the Udaya moun-tain shines due to the proximity of the sun similarly a person of a lower order becomes bright due to association with the people of the higher order (यथोदयगिरौ द्रव्यं संनिकर्षेण दीप्यते । तथा सत्संनिकर्-षेण हीनवर्णो ऽपि दीप्यते ॥ ) 12. 282. 4 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 293. 4: द्रव्यं मणिकाञ्चनादि दीप्यते सूर्यसन्निकर्षेण अत एव सन्ध्योः सूर्यरश्मयो द्रव्यप्र-भाविच्छुरणाद् रक्ता दृश्यन्ते). [See Udyant]
उद्यत्: Udyant m.: Name of a mountain. Described as resounding with songs (गीतनादित) 3. 82. 81; on this mountain are located Sāvitrapada (सावित्रं तु पदं तत्र) and the famous Yonidvāra (योनि-द्वारं च तत्रैव विश्रुतम्) 3. 82. 81, 83; if a Brāhmaṇa, of strict vows, performed संध्या on this mountain it was as good as performing it for twelve years (उपास्ता च भवेत् संध्या तेन द्वादशवार्षिकी) 3. 82. 82. [See Udaya]
उद्यन्त्: Udyant m.: Name of a mountain. Described as resounding with songs (गीतनादित) 3. 82. 81; on this mountain are located Sāvitrapada (सावित्रं तु पदं तत्र) and the famous Yonidvāra (योनि-द्वारं च तत्रैव विश्रुतम्) 3. 82. 81, 83; if a Brāhmaṇa, of strict vows, performed संध्या on this mountain it was as good as performing it for twelve years (उपास्ता च भवेत् संध्या तेन द्वादशवार्षिकी) 3. 82. 82. [See Udaya]
उपजला: Upajalā f.: Name of a river. Flowing near Yamunā (उपजलां चैव यमुनाम् अभितो नदीम्); king Uśīnara, having offered a sacrifice there, surpassed Indra 3. 130. 17.
उपरिगिरि: Uparigiri m.: Name (?) of a mountain. Situated in the north; Arjuna conquered it 2. 24. 2, 1.
उपेन्द्रा: Upendrā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 26, 5; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 13; all these rivers are mothers of the universe (विश्वस्य मातरः) and are very strong (महाबलाः) 6. 10. 35.
उर्वशी: Urvaśī f.: Name of a river (?) If one, who is well composed, goes to Urvaśī under the constellation Kṛttikā and bathes there in the Lauhitya तीर्थ according to the rites, he obtains the fruit of the Punḍa-rīka sacrifice (उर्वशीकृत्तिकायोगे गत्वा यः सुसमाहितः । लौहित्ये विधिवत् स्नात्वा पुण्डरीकफलं लभेत्) 13. 26. 43; (for Urvaśī as one of the names of Gaṅgā, see 12. 29. 61).
उर्वशीतीर्थ: Urvaśītīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated between Kālikāsaṅgama and Somāśrama 3. 82. 136 (135).
उशीरबीज: Uśīrabīja m.: Name of a mountain. Situated in the north (5. 109. 19-20) near Maināka and Śveta mountains which the Pāṇḍavas crossed in the company of Lomaśa 3. 140. 1; the mountain has a lake Jāmbū-nada; it was here that the king Marutta offered a sacrifice 5. 109. 20.
उत्तङ्काश्रम: Uttaṅkāśrama m.: Name of the hermi-tage of the great seer Uttaṅka. Situated near the delightful sandy desert, the sea full of sand, called Ujjānaka (महर्षिर् विश्रुतस् तात उत्तङ्क ईति भारत । मरुधन्वसु रम्येषु आश्रमस् तस्य कौरव ॥ ) 3. 192. 8; (ममाश्रमसमीपे वै समेषु मरुधन्वसु) 3. 193. 14; (समुद्रो वालुकापूऋण उज्जानक इति स्मृतः) 3. 195. 7; the demon Dhundhu lived under-ground, concealed by sand, and oppressed from there the hermitage of Uttaṅka by breathing out flames of fire (स दुष्टात्मा … बाधते स्म परं शक्त्या तम् उत्तङ्का-श्रमं प्रभो । … धुन्धुर् भीमपराक्र-मः ॥ शेते … उत्तङ्कस्याश्रमाभ्याशे निः-श्वसन् पावकार्चिषः ॥ ) 3. 195. 7-9; 3. 193. 14-17.
उत्तरज्योतिक: Uttarajyotika nt.: Name of a town (?) Nakula in his expedition to the west before the Rājasūya brought Uttarajyotika, along with the town Vṛndāṭaka, under his control (उत्तरज्योतिकं चैव तथा वृन्दा-टकम् पुरम् । … वशे चक्रे) 2. 29. 10.
उदयेन्दु: Udayendu nt.: Name of a city. A city of the Kurus (Pāṇḍavas); Suta-soma, son of Bhīma from Draupadī, was born there while there arose the sound of the pounding of Soma plants (?); hence called Sutasoma (पुरे कुरूणाम् उदयेन्दुनाम्नि । तस्मिञ् जातः सोमसंक्रन्दमध्ये यस्मात् तस्मात् सुतसोमो ऽभवत् सः ॥ ) 7. 22. 22 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 7. 23. 29 identifies Uda-yendu with Śakraprastha: तस्मिन् उदयेदु-नाम्नि उदयेन्दुपर्याये पुरे शक्रप्रस्थ एव । सोमसंक्रन्दः सोमाभिषवणं तस्य मध्ये तम् अधिकृत्य तत्फेनेनेत्य् अर्थः । ). [See Indraprastha]
उपप्लव्य: Upaplavya nt.: Name of the town near the capital of Virāṭa; called नगर 4. 67. 38; ग्राम 5. 22. 1. Epic events: (1) At the end of the thirteenth year, the Pāṇḍavas gathered to-gether at Upaplavya of Virāṭa and settled down there (ततस् त्रयोदशे वर्षे निवृत्ते पञ्च पाण्डवाः । उपप्लव्ये विराटस्य सम-पद्यन्त सर्वशः ॥ ) 4. 67. 14; (उपप्लव्ये निविष्टः … युधिष्ठिरः) 5. 142. 4; (2) While living there, Arjuna brought to Upa-plavya, Janārdana, Abhimanyu and the Dāśārhas from the Ānarta country; many other kings also assembled there; Abhi-manyu's marriage with Uttarā took place at Upaplavya 4. 67. 15-19, 25, 34; the city at that time shone as in a great festival and became full of people who were delighted and well nourished (तन् महोत्सवसंकाशं हृष्टपुष्तजनावृतम् । नगरं मत्स्यरा-जस्य शुशुभे भरतर्षभ ॥ ) 4. 67. 38; (3) When the Pāṇḍavas were settled in Upaplavya (उपप्लव्ये निविष्टेषु पाण्डवेषु), Duryodhana from Hāstinapura and Arjuna from Upaplavya went independently to see Vāsudeva to seek his help in the battle as they wished to win victory 1. 2. 136 (this is mentioned in the contents of the Udyoga-parvan which is a reference to 5. 7. 2-20); (4) After Duryodhana succeeded in trick-ing Śalya and in extracting a promise from him to fight from his side, the latter went to Upaplavya to report to the Pāṇḍavas what had happened 5. 8. 15; (5) When Dhṛta-rāṣṭra was informed that the Pāṇḍavas had resorted to Upaplavya, he sent Saṃjaya to greet them and to seek peace with them (प्राप्तान् आहुः संजय पाण्डुपुत्रान् उप-प्लव्ये) 5. 22. 1; 5. 22. 36; Saṃjaya, ac-cordingly, went to Upaplavya to meet the Pāṇḍavas (उपप्लव्यं ययौ द्रष्टुम्) 5. 23. 1; (6) Janārdana went from Upaplavya to Hāstinapura to negotiate peace with the Kauravas: on way he had encamped at Vṛkasthala (उपप्लव्याद् इह … उपयातो जनार्दनः । वृकस्थले निवसति) 5. 84. 1; (उपप्लव्याच् छान्तिम् इच्छञ् जनार्दनः । आगतः) 7. 61. 21; on Kṛṣṇa's way from Upaplavya to Hāstinapura people gathered in different towns to see him 5. 82. 18; Kṛṣṇa, without achieving his purpose, returned to Upaplavya when the sun arose (उच्चैःसूर्यम्) and reported to the Pāṇḍavas what happened at Hāstinapura 5. 135. 30; 5. 145. 1; (यदैवाकृतकार्यस् त्वम् उपप्लव्यं गतः पुनः) 11. 25. 31; (स गत्वा हास्तिनपुरं धृतराष्ट्रम् सम्-एत्य च … । अनवाप्य शमं तत्र कृष्णः … । आगच्छत महाबाहुर् उपप्लव्यम् … ॥ ) 9. 34. 5-7; (7) When Kṛṣṇa arrived at Upa-plavya, Yudhiṣṭhira offered him मधुपर्क and requested him to protect Arjuna in the battle (उपयातम् उपप्लव्यम् … एष भ्राता सखा चैव तव कृष्ण धनंजयः । रक्षितव्यो महाबाहो सर्वास्व् आपत्स्व् इति प्रभो ॥ ) 9. 61. 23-24 (No such specific request is reported earlier in the Udyoga-parvan; a general request by Yudhiṣṭhira to protect all the Pāṇḍavas is, however, repor-ted at 5. 70. 4); (8) While at Upaplavya, Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana had assured Yudhi-ṣṭhira that victory would be on that side which was helped by Kṛṣṇa (यतः कृष्णस् ततो जयः) 9. 61. 30; (such a statement by Vyāsa is not found earlier in the Ud-yogaparvan; however, such statement was made by Saṃjaya to Dhṛtaraṣṭra in Hāstina-pura 5. 66. 9 and by Nārada to Arjuna 6. 21. 12, 14; what Vyāsa told Dhṛtarāṣṭra was यतो धर्मस् ततो जयः 6. 2. 14; (9) Kṛṣṇa, along with the Pāṇḍavas, left Upaplavya for Kurukṣetra 9. 34. 14; when the Pāṇḍavas with their army started for the battlefield, Draupadī returned to Upapla-vya; before leaving, the Pāṇḍavas made arrangements for the defence of their base at Upaplavya by erecting forts and stationing troops all around (उपप्लव्ये तु पाञ्चाली  … निववृते) 5. 149. 55; (कृत्वा मूलप्रती-कारान् गुल्मैः स्थावरजङ्गमैः) 5. 149. 56 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 151. 61: मूलप्रती-कारं धनदाररक्षां गुल्मैः स्थावरैः प्राकाररूपैः जङ्गमैः परितः स्थाने स्थाने शूरसङ्घैः); (10) Balarāma did not agree to Kṛṣṇa's request to him to help the Pāṇḍavas in the battle and left from Upaplavya for a pilgrimage 9. 34. 10-12; (11) During the battle Kṛṣṇa, at one stage, in order to encourage Yudhiṣṭhira reminded him that Arjuna had taken the vow at Upaplavya to bring about the down-fall of Bhīṣma (प्रतिज्ञातम् उपप्लव्ये यत् तत् पार्थेन … घातयिष्यामि गाङ्गेयम्) 6. 103. 35 (a reference to 5. 160. 8, 12, 13; 5, 162. 1); (12) At the end of the war Nakula went to fetch Draupadī who was at Upa-plavya; she was afflicted when she heard the extremely sad news about the destruction of all her sons (उपप्लव्यगता सा तु श्रुत्वा सुमहद् अप्रियम्) 10. 11. 4-5; she taunt-ingly said to Arjuna that while living with her at Upaplavya he would happily forget his sons who were slain rightfully (in battle) (आत्मजांस् तेन धर्मेण श्रुत्वा शूरान् निपातितान् । उपप्लव्ये मया सार्धं दिष्ट्या त्वं न स्मरिष्यसि) 10. 11. 12; (13) A cer-tain Brāhmaṇa, observing vows, after seeing Uttarā at Upaplavya had foretold that when the Kurus were destroyed (परिक्षीण) a son would be born to her; the child thus would have the nature परिक्षित् while he was still in the womb (विराटस्य सुताम् … । उपप्लव्यगतां दृष्ट्वा व्रतवान् ब्राह्मणो ऽब्रवीत् ॥ परिक्षिणेषु कुरुषु पुत्रस् तव जनिष्यति । एतद् अस्य परिक्षित्त्वम् गर्भस्-थस्य भविष्यति ॥ ) 10. 16. 2-3.
उपमन्योर्: Upamanyor āśramaḥ m.: The आश्रम of Upamanyu. A. Location: The आश्रम of Upamanyu Vaiyāghrapadya (son of Vyāghrapāda 13. 14. 75) on Himavant (तत्र … गिरिसत्तमे आश्रअमम् … वैयाघ्रपद्यस्य उपमन्योः) 13. 14. 27-28. B. Description: Best (श्रेष्ठ) 13. 14. 43, (उत्तम) 13. 14. 27; delightful to all beings (सर्वभूतमनो-रम) 13. 14. 43; heavenly (दिव्य) 13. 14. 28; everything in the hermitage was end-owed with heavenly aspect (सर्वम् एतन् … दिव्यभावसमन्वितम्) 13. 14. 199; the like of the आश्रम cannot even be imagined by others (अचिन्त्यं मनसाप्य् अन्यैः) 13. 14. 36; covered by sacred splendour (ब्राह्म्या लक्ष्म्या समन्वितम्) 13. 14. 28; the best place for practising austerities (क्षेत्रं च तपसां श्रेष्ठम्) 13. 14. 27; adorned by great sages who were like fire (महर्षिभिर् भूषितम् अग्निकल्पैः) 13. 14. 37; 13. 14. 198; excellent Brāhmaṇas observing in the आश्र-मस् different kinds of very difficult vows; their vows are detailed in 13. 14. 38-40; very learned Brāhmaṇas versed in the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas took resort to it (सेविते द्विज-शार्दूलैर् वेदवेदाङ्गपारगैः) 13. 14. 43; resorted to by high-souled sages famous for observing various restrictions (नानानिय-मविख्यातैर् ऋषिभिश् च महात्मभिः) 13. 14. 44; adorned with large places of sacri-ficial fire (विशालैश् चाग्निशरणैर् भूषितम्) 13. 14. 36; covered with कुश grass (कुश-संवृतम्) 13. 14. 36; honoured by hosts of high-souled gods, Śiva and others, the surroundings of the hermitage shone at all times like the orb of the sun in the sky (सुपूजितं देवगणैर् महात्मभिः शिवादिभिर् … रराज तच् चाश्रममण्डलं सदा दिवीव राजन् रविमण्डलं यथा) 13. 14. 41; honoured by gods and Gan-dharvas (पूजितं देवगन्धर्वैः) 13. 14. 28; Siddhas, Vidyādharas, Yakṣas and Apsarases also present there 13. 14. 198; adorned and always liked by the river Gaṅgā (विभूषितं … सदा च जुष्टं नृप जह्नुकन्यया) 13. 14. 37; adorned on all sides by lakes (सरोभिः समलंकृतम्) 13. 14. 36; full of all kinds of forest trees yielding flowers and fruits (वन्यैर् बहु-विधैर् वृक्षैः फलपुष्पप्रदैर् युतम्) 13. 14. 31 (the trees like धव, ककुभ कदम्ब etc. are listed in 13. 14. 29-30); adorned by trees and fruits to be enjoyed by birds (नानाशकुनीसंभोज्यैः फलैर् वृक्षैर् अलंकृतम्) 13. 14. 32; having attractive trees, always full of flowers and fruits, covered with flowers of all seasons, having glossy leaves and large branches (पश्य वृक्षान् मनोरम्यान् सदा पुष्प-फलान्वितान् । सर्वर्तुकुसुमैर् युक्तान् स्नि-ग्धपत्रान् सुशाखिनः) 13. 14. 199; thick with flowering thickets and creepers and adorned with clusters of कदली trees (पुष्प-गुल्मलताकीर्णं कदलीषण्दशोभितम्) 13. 14. 31; adorned with rows of trees placed in their proper order (यथास्थानविनिक्षि-प्तैर् भूषितं वनराजिभिः) 13. 14. 32; it was full of different kinds of animals like Ruru antelopes, elephants, lions, tigers, leopards, peacocks, cats, serpents, buffaloes and bears 13. 14. 33; one special feature of the आश्रम was that due to the prowess of the austerities (of its ascetics) ichneu-mons played with serpents, and tigers with deer, like friends (क्रीडन्ति सर्पैर् नकुला मृगैर् व्याघ्राश् च मित्रवत् । प्रभावाद् दीप्ततपसः) 13. 14. 42; wind, mixed with the pollen of various flowers and carrying with it the scent of the rut of the elephants and thick with songs of heavenly women blew there (नानापुष्परजोमिश्रो गजदाना-धिवासितः । दिव्यस्त्रीगीतबहुलो मारुतो ऽत्र सुखं ववौ ॥ ) 13. 14. 34; one could also hear other sounds as those of waterfalls, of birds, of trumpetings, of elephants, of songs of Kiṃnaras and of Sāman-singers 13. 14. 35. C. Presence of Śiva: As a boon Upamanyu asked Śiva to be always near him in his आश्रम; that boon was granted by Śiva (आश्रमे च सदा मह्यं सांनि-ध्यं परम् अस्तु ते । … सांनिध्यम् आश्रमे नित्यं करिष्यामि द्विजोत्तम) 13. 14. 189, 194.
उरशा: Uraśā f.: Name of a city. Arjuna in his expedition to the north defeated Rocamāna living at Uraśā in the north-west (उरशावासिनं चैव रोचमानं रणे ऽजयत्) 2. 24. 18.
उलूकाश्रम: Ulūkāśrama m.: Name of an आश्रम। Established by the sage Ulūka; des-cribed as auspicious (शुभ) 5. 187. 25; the Kāśī princess Ambā, while practising aus-terities for the death of Bhīṣma, visited many holy places, one of them being Ulūkā-śrama; she bathed at these holy places day and night and practised austerities (तत्र पुण्येषु देशेषु साप्लुताङ्गी दिवानिशम् । व्य-वचरत् काशिकन्या सा … ॥ … ततोलूकाश्रमे शुभे) 5. 187. 24-25; (एतेषु तीर्थेषु तदा काशिकन्या … आप्लावयत गात्राणि तीव्रम् आस्थाय वै तपः) 5. 187. 28.
उत्कल: Utkala m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. (1) Listed by Saṃjaya among the (northern) Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (मेकलाश् चोत्कलैः सह) 6. 10. 39. (2) In the epic war they, along with Mekalas and others, showered arrows and तोमरस् on Nakula to kill him (मेकलोत्कलकालिङ्गा … । शरतोमरवर्-षाणि विमुञ्चन्तो जिघांसवः ॥ तैश् छाद्य-मानं नकुलम्) 8. 17. 20-21.
उत्तम: Uttama m. (pl.): Name of a people ? Bhīma in his expedition to the east, south and north (ययौ प्राचीं दिशं प्रति 2. 26. 1; ततः प्राचीं दिशं भीमो ययौ 2. 26. 7; ततो दक्षिणम् आगम्य 2. 26. 10; ततो हिमवतः पार्श्वे 2. 27. 4) conquered the Uttamas when he went beyond Ayo-dhyā and Gopālakaccha and then to the foot of the Himālayas (ततो गोपालकच्छं च सोत्तमान् अपि चोत्तरान् … व्यजयत् प्र-भुः) 2. 27. 3; (since in 2. 27. 11 there is a reference to Dakṣiṇamallas, and in 2. 27. 3 मल्लानाम् अधिपं चैव follows immedi-ately after सोत्तमान् अपि चोत्तरान्, it is very likely that उत्तरान् and उत्तमान् refer to the northern and most northern Mallas; the passage would then mean that Bhīma conquered the king of Mallas, together with the Uttara and Uttama Mallas; Edgerton, however, takes Uttara and Uttama as names of different peoples, see his note on this stanza in Cr. Ed. Vol. II, p. 501).
उत्तमौज: Uttamauja m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada (or Uttamaujas sg. ?) Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; (उत्तमौजा दशार्णाश् च) 6. 10. 39.
उत्तरकुरु: Uttarakuru m. (pl.): Name of a द्वीप and of the people residing there. A. Location: Counted by Saṃjaya among the four द्वीपस् on the four sides of mountain Meru (तस्य (i. e. of mount Meru 6. 7. 8) पार्श्वे त्व् इमे द्वीपाश् चत्वारः सं-स्थिताः प्रभो । … उत्तराश् चैव कुरवः) 6. 7. 11; to the south of Nīla mountain and to the northern side of mount Meru (दक्षि-णेन तु नीलस्य मेरोः पार्श्वे तथोत्तरे । उत्तरा कुरवो राजन्) 6. 8. 2; the river which arises from the juice of the fallen fruit of Jambū tree makes a प्रदक्षिणा of Meru and flows to the Uttara Kurus (तस्या जम्-ब्वाः फलरसो नदी भूत्वा जनाधिप । मेरुं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा संप्रयात्य् उत्तरान् कुरून् ॥ ) 6. 8. 23; it lies beyond the countries occupied by Mlecchas, and beyond the mountainous regions occupied by Vidyādharas, Vānaras, Kiṃnaras, Kiṃ-puruṣas; beyond the Uttara Kurus lie the Kailāsa mountain and the Naranārāyaṇā-śrama (देशान् म्लेच्छगणाकीर्णान् … ददृशुर् गिरिपादांश् च … विद्याधरगणाकीर्णान् युतान् वानरकिंनरैः । तथा किंपुरुषैश् चैव गन्धर्वैश् च समन्ततः ॥ … ते व्यतीत्य बहून् देशान् उत्तरांश् च कुरून् अपि । ददृशुर् … कैलासं पर्वतोत्तमम् ॥ तस्याभ्याशे तु ददृशुर् नरनारायणाश्र-मम् (3. 145. 12-13; 15-16; they are con-ceived to be beyond mountain Meru and the Nandana forest and below the world of Soma 13. 105. 20, 23, 29; Arjuna in his expedition to the north went up to the Uttara Kurus but did not enter it; the Uttara Kurus lay beyond the Śveta mountain, the residence of Kiṃpuruṣas, the Hāṭaka deśa, Gandharva deśa, Hari-varṣa in the north (प्रययाव् उत्तरां तस्माद् दिशं) 2. 24. 1; (एवं स … विजिग्ये दिशं उत्तराम्) 2. 25. 17, 24; (स श्वेतपर्वतं वीरः समतिक्रम्य … दे-शं किंपुरुषावासम् … तं जित्वा हाटकं देशम् … गन्धर्वरक्षितं देशं व्यज-यत् पाण्डवस् ततः ॥ … उत्तरं हरिवर्-षं तु समासाद्य स पाण्डवः । … उत्तराः कुरवो ह्य् एते) 2. 25. 1, 3, 5, 7, 11; (दिशं ह्य् उदीचीम् अपि चोत्तरान् कुरून् गाण्डीव-धन्वा एकरथो जिगाय) 5. 22. 12; (accor-ding to Nīla. on Bom. Ed. 5. 22. 12: उत्तरान् कुरून् हिमाचलाद् अप्य् उदग्देशान् स्वर्ग-भूमिरूपान्); they are once distinguished from the southern Kurus (i. e. the Kuru country) 1. 102. 10. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 6. 8. 2; 13. 54. 16; delightful (रम्य) 13. 105. 25; where Siddhas live (सिद्धनिषेवित) 6. 8. 2; abode of those who have done meritorious acts (कृतपुण्य-प्रतिश्रय) 6. 7. 11. C. Holiness: (1) The land of the Uttara Kurus was meant for those who had no expectations from all beings, who did not eat meat, who had abandoned the use of rod, who did no injury to moving and non-moving beings, who had become one with all beings, who had no desires, no attachments, who were free from passions, who were indifferent to gain and loss, to abuse and praise (ये सर्वभूतेषु निवृत्तकामा अमांसादा न्यस्-तदण्डाश् चरन्ति । न हिंसन्ति स्थावरं जङ्गमं च भूतानां ये सर्वभूतात्म-भूताः ॥ निराशिषो निर्ममा वीतरागा लाभा-लाभे तुल्यनिन्दाप्रशंसाः । तथाविधा-नाम् एष लोको महर्षे) 13. 105. 27-28; (2) One who donates household articles (like bed etc.), having all qualities, to a good Brāhmaṇa, who is learned and virtu-ous, goes to the land of the Uttara Kurus (नैवेशिकं सर्वगुणोपपन्नम् ददाति वै यस् तु नरो द्विजाय । स्वाध्यायचारित्रगुणान्-विताय तस्यापि लोकाः कुरुषूत्तरेषु ॥ ) 13. 57. 33 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 57. 33: नैवेशिकं गृहोपस्करं शय्यादि); (3) Warriors who somehow got killed between two battles in the epic war went to Uttara Kurus (ये तत्र निहता राजन्न् अन्तरायो-धनं प्रति । यथाकथंचित् ते राजन् संप्राप्ता उत्तरान् कुरून्) 11. 26. 17. D. Characteristics: (1) The trees in the Uttara Kurus have sweet and juicy fruits and fragrant flowers; they bear fruits and flowers in all seasons; some trees give any kind of fruit according to one's desire and others always yield milk which has six flavours and is like अमृत; they also produce garments and ornaments from their fruits; jewelled ground in the Uttara Kurus is spread over with thin golden sand; it is everywhere pleasant to touch and is free from mud; men who fall down from the world of gods are born there; both men and women there have similar form and virtues; they are born in pairs; the women are comparable with अप्सरस्; they drink milk, which is like अमृत, of the milk-producing trees; since they are born in pairs, they grow up to-gether, are similar in form and virtues and wear similar dress; they love each other like the चक्रवाक birds; they are always happy and live ten thousand and ten hundr-ed years; free from disease, they are not afflicted by sorrow; they never abandon each other; when they die, very strong Bhāruṇḍa birds, having sharp beaks, carry them away and throw them in valleys; (this is a short description of the Uttarakurus given by Saṃjaya to Dhṛtarāṣṭra) (उत्तरा कुरवो राजन् … । तत्र वृक्षा मधुफला नित्य-पुष्पफलोपगाः । पुष्पाणि च सुगन्धीनि रसवन्ति फलानि च ॥ सर्वकामफलास् तत्र केचिद् वृक्षा जनाधिप । अपरे क्षीरिणो नाम वृक्षास् तत्र नराधिप ॥ ये क्षरन्ति सदा क्षीरं षड्रसं ह्य् अमृतोपमम् । वस्त्राणि च प्रसूयन्ते फलेष्व् आभरणानि च ॥ सर्वा मणिमया भूमिः सूक्ष्म-काञ्चनवालुका । सर्वत्र सुखसंस्पर्शा निष्पङ्का च जनाधिप ॥ देवलोकच्युताः सर्वे जायन्ते तत्र मानवाः । तुल्यरूप-गुणोपेताः समेषु विषमेषु च ॥ मिथुनानि च जायन्ते स्त्रियश् चाप्सरसोपमाः । तेषां ते क्षीरिणां क्सीरम् पिबन्त्य् अमृतशंनि-भम् ॥ मिथुनं जायमानं वै समं तच् च प्रवर्धते । तुल्यरूपगुणोपेतं समवेषं तथैव च । एकैकम् अनु-रक्तं च चक्रवाकसमं विभो ॥ नीरा-मया वीतशोका नित्यं मुदितमानसाः । दश वर्षसहस्राणि दश वर्षशतानि च । जीवन्ति ते महाराज न चान्योन्यं जहत्य् उत ॥ भारुण्डा नाम शकुनास् तीक्ष्णतुण्डा महाबलाः । ते निर्हरन्ति हि मृतान् दरीषु प्रक्षिपन्ति च ॥ उत्तरा कुरवो राजन् व्या-ख्यातास् ते समासतः । ) 6. 8. 2-12; (2) The juicy fruits of the Jambū tree called Sudarśana, falling on ground, give rise to a river which, after encircling the Meru mountain, flows to the Uttarakurus; the men living in the Uttarakurus happily drink that juice and hence oldage never over-takes them (तस्मिन् फलरसे पीते न जरा बाधते च तान्) 6. 8. 23-24; (3) At the birth of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu and Vidura, the people of the Kuru country became so pros-perous and happy that they are said to have vied with the people of the Uttara Kurus (उत्तरैः कुरुभ्त्ः सार्धं दक्षिणाः कुर-वस् तदा । विस्पर्धमाना व्यचरन्) 1. 102. 10; (4) In the Uttarakurus, Brāhmaṇas who are not born the natural way, i. e. whose origin is in the fire or mountain, de-light with gods (देवैः सार्धं मोदमाना नरेन्द्र । यत्राग्नियौनाश् च वसन्ति विप्रा ह्य् अयोनयः पर्वतयोनयश् च) 13. 105. 25 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 102. 25: अग्नियौना धृष्टद्युम्नवद् अग्निर् एव यौनं योनिर् येषां ते); (5) King Kuśika having seen the golden palace, looking like the Gandharvanagara, and the wonderful forest created by sage Cyavana wondered whether he was bodily transferred to the land of the Uttarakurus (अहो सह शरीरेण प्राप्तो ऽस्मि परमां गतिम् । उत्तरान् वा कुरून् पुण्यान्) 13. 54 16, 1-2; (6) Indra showers all wishes on this land (यत्रोत्तराः कुरवो … यत्र शक्रो वर्षति सर्वकामान्) 13. 105. 25-26; (7) The gate-keepers of Harivarṣa told Arjuna that those were the lands of the Uttarakurus and he could not conquer their town; one who entered it did not remain a man: no wars were fought on the lands of Uttarakurus; even if Arjuna entered the land he would not be able to see anything, since no one with a human body could see anything there (तत एनं  … द्वारपाला समासाद्य … वचनम् अब्रु-वन् ॥ पार्थ नेदं त्वया शक्यं पुरं जेतुं कथंचन । … इदं पुरं यः प्रविशेद् ध्रुवं स न भवेन् नरः । … उत्तराः कुरवो ह्य् एते नात्र युद्धं प्र-वर्तते ॥ प्रविष्टश् चापि कौन्तेय नेह द्रक्ष्यसि किंचन । न हि मानुषदेहेन शक्यम् अत्राभिवीक्षितुम् ॥ ) 2. 25. 8-12; (8) Formerly, women were not closet-ed (in four walls), they moved as they liked, and were independent; they united with men other than their husbands since their marriage as virgins, and in ancient times that was not अधर्म, but धर्म; that ancient धर्म, favourable to wo-men, was still practised by people of the Uttara Kurus (अनावृताः किल पुरा स्त्रिय आसन् वरानने । कामचारविहारिण्यः स्व-तन्त्राश् चारुलोचने ॥ तासां व्युच्चरमा-णानाम् कौमारात् सुभगे पतीन् । नाधर्मो ऽभूत् वरारोहे स हि धर्मः पुराभवत् ॥  … पुराणदृष्टो धर्मो ऽयम् … उत्तरेषु च रम्भोरु कुरुष्व् अद्यापि वर्तते ॥ ) 1. 113. 4-5, 6-7; (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 122. 4: अनावृताः सर्वैर् द्रष्टुं योग्याः । काम-चारो रतिसुखं तदर्थं विहारिण्यः पर्-यटनशीलाः स्वतन्त्राः भर्त्रादिभिर् अनि-वार्याः । ); where women behaved as they liked, where men and women were not envi-ous (यत्र स्त्रियः कामचाराश् चरन्ति । यत्र चेर्ष्या नास्ति नारीनराणाम्) 13. 105. 26. E. Epic events: (1) Pāṇḍu told Kuntī that the ancient धर्म, applicable to married women, was still followed among the Uttarakurus 1. 113. 7 (see above D. Characteristics: No. 7). (2) The gate-keepers of Harivarṣa did not allow Arjuna to enter the town (see above D. Characteri-stics No. 6); they advised Arjuna to return; he then told gate-keepers that he would not enter the land that was prohibited for human beings; he however asked for tri-bute for Yudhiṣṭhira's Rājasūya sacrifice; the gate-keepers then gave Arjuna heavenly garments, ornaments and animal- and deer-skins (न प्रवक्ष्यामि वो देशं बाध्यत्वं यदि मानुषैः । युधिष्ठिराय यत् किंचित् करवन् नः प्रदीयताम् ॥ ततो दिव्यानि वस्त्राणि दिव्यान्य् आभरणानि च । मोकाजिनानि दिव्यानि तस्मै ते प्रददुः करम् ॥ ) 2. 25. 15-16; Dhṛtarāṣṭra referred to Arjuna's conquering the northern direc-tion and the Uttarakurus and making them pay tribute; he also said that Arjuna brought wealth from them and made them join his army (which is not reported earlier in 2. 25. 15-16) (दिशम् उदीचीम् अपि चोत्त-रान् कुरून् गाण्डीवधन्वा … जिगाय । धनं चैषाम् आहरत् सव्यसाची सेनानुगान् बलि-दांश् चैव चक्रे) 5. 22. 12; (3) Flowers, brought down by waters flowing from Uttarakurus, were brought for making garlands as tribute to Yudhiṣṭhira by the mountain peoples (उत्तरेभ्यः कुरुभ्यश् चाप्य् अपोढं माल्यम् अम्बुभिः । … पार्व-तीया बलिं चान्यम् आहृत्य प्रणताः स्थिताः) 2. 48. 6-7; (4) The Pāṇḍavas on their way to Gandhamādana crossed the Uttara-kurus and saw the Kailāsa mountain and the आश्रम of Nara and Nārāyaṇa in its vicinity (ते व्यतीत्य … उत्तरांश् च कुरून् अपि । ददृशुर् … कैलासम् … ॥ तस्याभ्याशे तु ददृशुर् नरनारायणाश्रमम्) 3. 145. 15-16; (5) After the miracle of the meeting of the dead warriors with their living relatives, brought about by Vyāsa, the dead returned to the place from where they came; some of them returned to the Uttarakurus (स्वानि स्थानानि भेजिरे ॥ ॥।केचिच् चाप्य् उत्तरान् कुरून्) 15. 41. 13, 15. F. Past events: The sage Gautama offered king Dhṛtarāṣṭra (who was really Indra) the world of the Uttarakurus in lieu of his elephant but the latter refused to re-turn the elephant and accept the Uttarakurus (यत्रोत्तराः कुरवो भान्ति रम्या … तत्र त्वाहं हस्तिनं यातयिष्ये ॥ … परं गन्ता धृतराष्ट्रो न तत्र) 13. 105. 25-26, 28; (2) In the long, twelve-yearly sacrifice of the sage Agastya, when a difficulty arose due to famine, the sage just said that what-ever wealth was found in the Uttarakurus all that should appear of its own accord at the place of his sacrifice, and it happened just as he said (उत्तरेभ्यः कुरुभ्यश् च यत् किंचिद् वसु विद्यते । सर्वं तद् थ यज्ञे मे स्वयम् एवोपतिष्ठतु । … इत्य् उक्ते सर्वम् एवैतद् अभवत् तस्य धीमतः) 14. 95. 25-26.
उत्तरापथ: Uttarāpatha m. (pl.): General desig-nation of the northern Bhārata and its peoples. A. Peoples: Among the peoples born in the Uttarāpatha (उत्तरापथजन्मानः), Bhīṣma listed Yaunas, Kāmbojas, Gāndhā-ras, Kirātas and Barbaras 12. 200. 40. B. Description of the above people: Skilled in the use of all kinds of weapons and missiles (सर्वशस्त्रास्त्रकुशलाः) 6. 16. 17; sinful, leading the life of dogs, crows, बलस् (a kind of crow ?), and vultures, they roam all over this earth; they did not exist in the Kṛtayuga but were to be met with since the Tretāyuga (एते पापकृतस् तात चरन्ति पृथि-वीम् इमाम् । श्वकाकबलगृध्राणां सध-र्माणो नराधिप ॥ नैते कृतयुगे तात चरन्ति पृथिवीम् इमाम् । त्रेताप्रभृति वर्तन्ते ते जना … ) 12. 200. 41-42. C. Epic event: Duryodhana told Duḥśāsana that, among others, the warriors from the Uttarāpatha were to protect Bhīṣma (दाक्षि-णात्योत्तरापथाः । … ते रक्षन्तु पिता-महम्) 6. 16. 17.
उत्स: Utsa m. (pl.): Name of a people from the Dakṣiṇāpatha. A. Location: They are counted with Talavaras, Andhrakas and others as natives of the Dakṣiṇāpatha (दक्षिणापथजन्-मानः सर्वे तलवरान्ध्रकाः । उत्साः … ) 12. 200. 39. B. Description: They are described as those who do not believe in Bhūtapati as the superintendent of all beings (निरध्यक्षाः) 12. 200. 38; they are sinful and lead the life of dogs, crows, बलष् (a kind of crow ?) and vultures; they roam all over this earth; they did not exist in Kṛtayuga, but were to be found from Tretā-yuga onwards 12. 200. 41-42 (for citation see above Uttarāpatha).
उत्सवसंकेत: Utsavasaṃketa m. (pl.): Name of a Gaṇa. A. Location: Two settlements of them: (1) To the north of Khāṇḍavaprastha (प्रययाव् उत्तरां दिशम्) 2. 24. 1; near Kashmīra (ततः काश्मीरकान् वीरान् … व्यज-यत्) 2. 24. 16; (2) Those who lived to the west of Khāṇḍavaprastha (निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम्) 2. 29. 2; in the Puṣkara forest (पुष्करा-रण्यवासिनः) 2. 29. 7. B. Dasyus: They formed a class of Dasyus living on moun-tains (दस्यून् पर्वतवासिनः) 2. 24. 15. C. Number: Seven Gaṇas of them (गणान् सप्त) 2. 24. 15. D. Epic events: (1) Arjuna in his expedition to the north before the Rājasūya conquered them (गणान् उत्सवसंकेतान् अजयत् सप्त पाण्डवः) 2. 24. 15; (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 27. 16: उत्-सवसंकेतान् स्त्रीपुंसयोः परस्परप्रीतिर् एव रत्यर्थं संकेतः न तु दांपत्य-व्यवस्था पशूनाम् इव यत्रास्तीत्य् अर्थः); (2) Nakula in his expedition to the west before the Rājasūya conquered them (गणान् उत्स्वसंकेतान् व्यजयत् पुरुष-र्षभः) 2. 29. 8 [See Dhvajinyutsavasaṃ-keta].
उदीच्य: Udīcya m. (pl.): General characteri-zation of northern people. A. Description: Not cruel (अनृशंस), brave (शूर), distinguished for their good character and conduct (शीलवृत्तोपपन्न) 5. 30. 24. B. Epic events: (1) Yudhi-ṣṭhira asked Saṃjaya to wish good health to northern kings who, among others, were gathered by Duryodhana to fight with the Pāṇḍavas (ये राजानः पाण्डवायोधनाय समानीता धार्तराष्ट्रेण केचित् । … प्राच्यो-दीच्या … तेषां सर्वेषां कुशलं तात पृच्छेः ॥ ) 5. 30. 23-24; (2) Udīcyas mentioned among those who formed the second division of Duryodhana's army while leaving Hāstinapura for Kurukṣetra (प्राच्योदीच्याश् च सर्वशः । … एते महा-रथाः सर्वे द्वितीये निर्ययुर् बले) 5. 196. 7-8; (3) Sātyaki told Yudhiṣṭhira that the northern and the southern warriors were not equal to even the sixteenth part of angered Arjuna (उदीच्या दाक्षिणात्याश् च … एते ऽर्जुनस्य क्रुद्धस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम्) 7. 86. 28-29; (4) During the night war of the fourteenth day, when Śakuni, as instructed by Duryo-dhana, attacked the Pāṇḍavas to kill them, Udīcyas were to follow him (उदीच्याः कृत-वर्मा च … एते त्वाम् अनुयास्यन्ति) 7. 131. 84, 86; (5) On the seventeenth day of war, when Arjuna, as suggested by Kṛṣṇa, boasted of his exploits, he mentioned Udī-cyas among those who were killed by him (हता उदीच्या निहता प्रतीच्याः) 8. 49. 96; (6) At the end of the seventeenth day of the war, when Saṃjaya told Dhṛtarāṣṭra, all those that had fallen in the war at the hands of Arjuna, he mentioned Udīcyas among them (प्राच्योदीच्याः प्रतीच्याश् च … ते हता समरे राजन् पार्थेन) 8. 4. 47, 50; (7) At the end of the eighteenth day of war, Saṃjaya while reporting to Dhṛtarāṣṭra warriors who were killed on that day said that all Udīcyas were killed (उदीच्या निह-ताः सर्वे) 9. 1. 27.
उदीच्यभोज: Udīcyabhoja m. (pl.): Name of a people. Kṛṣṇa told Yudhiṣṭhira that the Udī-cyabhojas, along with eighteen other tribes resorted to the west due to the fear of Jarāsandha (उदीच्यभोजाश् च तथा कुलान्य् अष्टादशाभिभो । जरासन्धभयाद् एव प्रतीचीं दिशम् आश्रिताः ॥ ) 2. 13. 24.
उन्नत्यक: Unnatyaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the southern Janapadas (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 56, 5; also called the Deśas (देशाः संकीर्तिताः) 6. 10. 68; (उन्नत्यका माहिषका … ) 6. 10. 57.
उपत्यक: Upatyaka m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the (northern) Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्-वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; also called the Deśas (देशाः संकीर्तिताः) 6. 10. 68; (कुलिन्दोपत्यकास् तथा) 6. 10. 54.
उपावृश्च: Upāvṛśca m. (pl.): Name of a Jana-pada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपादान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; also called the Deśas (देशाः संकीर्तिताः) 6. 10. 68; (उपावृश्चानुपावृश्च-सुराष्ट्राः) 6. 10. 47.
उरग: Uraga m. pl.): Name of a Janapada ? Listed by Saṃjaya among the (nor-thern) Janapadas of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध गदतो मम) 6. 10. 37, 5; also called the Deśas (देशाः संकीर्तिताः) 6. 10. 68; (वातजामरथोर-गाः) 6. 10. 53 (or, do we read वातजाम-रथोरगाः ?)
उशीनर: Uśīnara m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Description: According to Bhīṣma they were spirited and skilled in the use of all kinds of weapons (सर्वशस्त्रेषु कुशलाः सत्त्ववन्तो ह्य् उशीनराः) 12. 102. 4. B. Degradation: Bhīṣma mentioned Uśīnaras among those who became Śūdras because they showed no respect for Brāhmaṇas (पुलिन्दाश् चाप्य् उशीनराः । … वृषलत्वं परिगता ब्राह्मणानाम् अदर्शनात्) 13. 33. 20-21 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 33. 21: अदर्श-नात् अननुग्रहात्). C. Epic event: Saṃjaya mentioned Uśīnaras among those who were killed by Arjuna on the seventeenth day of the war (क्षुद्रकाश् चाप्य् ऊशीनराः । … ते हताः समरे राजन् पार्थेन) 8. 4. 46, 50.
उष्ण: Uṣṇa m. (sg.): Name of a country in the Krauñcadvīpa. It lay beyond the country (देश) called Manonuga and beyond Uṣṇa lay Prāvaraka (देशांस् तत्र प्रवक्ष्यामि … मनोनुगात् परश् चोष्णो देशः … उष्णात् परः प्रावर-कः) 6. 13. 20-21; these Deśas were visited by gods and Gandharvas (एते देशा महा-राज देवगन्धर्वसेविताः) 6. 13. 23.
उद्वह: Udvaha m.: Name of the third of the seven winds. A. Divine origin: All the seven winds are Aditi's sons ( … एते ऽदितेः पुत्रा मारु-ताः … ) 12. 315. 53. B. Description: Most raining (वर्षिष्ठ) 12. 315. 40; all the seven winds are very wonderful, blow incessantly in all places sustaining all (creatures) (पर-माद्भुताः । अनारमन्तः संवान्ति सर्वगाः सर्वधारिणः) 12. 315. 53; (सदागति) 12. 315. 40; when it is inside the bodies it is called by great sages उदान (अन्तर्-देहेषु चोदानं यं वदन्ति महर्षयः) 12. 315. 38. C. Activity: It blows along the third of the seven paths of winds which blow on the earth and in the atmosphere (पृथिव्याम् अन्तरिक्षे च यत्र संवान्ति वायवः । सप्तैते वायुमार्गा वै … ) 12. 315. 31; (उद्वहो नाम तृतीयः स सदागतिः) 12. 315. 40; it causes moon and other luminaries to rise; it takes water from four oceans, holds it, and then gives it first to the clouds in the sky and next gives the watery clouds to Parjanya (उदयं ज्योति-षां शश्वत् सोमादीनां करोति यः । … यश् चतुर्भ्यः समुद्रेभ्यो वायुर् धारयते जलम् । उद्धृत्याददते चापो जीमूतेभ्यो ऽम्बरे ऽनिलः ॥ यो ऽद्भिः संयोज्य जीमूतान् पर्जन्याय प्रयच्छति । ) 12. 315. 38-40.
